mainTopic: רבי יהודה's view on intending to leave the blood until tomorrow, the story of יוסף הבבלי, and a new משנה about steps of the מנחה that do not make it פסולה.
overview: The גמרא explains the view that רבי אלעזר is arguing against. רבי יהודה holds that intending to leave some of the blood until tomorrow makes the קרבן פסול according to everyone, because of a rabbinic גזירה. רבי אלעזר says that even here רבי אליעזר says פסול and חכמים say כשר. The גמרא then questions whether רבי יהודה really holds 'everyone agrees'. It quotes a moving ברייתא: יוסף הבבלי kept asking רבי אלעזר בן שמוע about this case until he heard that רבי אליעזר says פסול, which 'returned his lost item'. After weighing both readings, the גמרא concludes that רבי יהודה did teach 'everyone agrees it is פסול', and יוסף was happy just to hear that some פסול view exists. A new משנה then lists steps of the מנחה whose absence does not make it פסולה. The גמרא begins explaining 'did not pour' as pouring done by a זר rather than a כהן, and shows that by the same reading, not mixing at all would make the מנחה פסולה.

steps.title: רבי יהודה limits the argument
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה holds that רבי אליעזר and חכמים argue only in the earlier cases. If the intent was to leave the blood until tomorrow, everyone agrees the offering is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה holds that they argue only in those cases. But if the intent is to leave it, everyone agrees it is unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the view of רבי יהודה. This view is the reason רבי אלעזר will need to make his statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, רבי אליעזר and חכמים argued about a person who slaughters a קרבן with a strange plan for it. רבי יהודה says that argument covers only those strange-use cases. A plan to simply leave the blood until tomorrow is different, and everyone agrees it makes the offering פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: To leave (the blood) until the next day

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'leaving' the blood with the earlier cases. In the earlier cases the person planned to use the offering in a strange way. Here he only plans to leave it until tomorrow.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda holds
they disagree in those cases,
phrases.notes: 'Those cases' are the ones just discussed, where the person planned to use the offering in an unusual way.

phrases.english: but to leave it – everyone agrees it is unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the earlier discussion of רבי אלעזר's statement 'אף בזו' and explains the opposing view he is responding to.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, intending to leave the blood until tomorrow makes the offering פסול according to everyone.

steps.title: Why is leaving the blood unfit?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבי יהודה's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question to set up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaving only some of the blood seems like a small thing, so why should everyone agree it is פסול? The גמרא wants the logic behind the rule.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the ruling in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason everyone agrees that intending to leave the blood makes the offering פסול.

steps.title: A rabbinic decree: some of the blood because of all of it
steps.stepSummary: Leaving some of the blood is פסול because of a rabbinic גזירה. חכמים worried people would confuse it with leaving all of the blood, which is פסול מדאורייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a decree about some of its blood because of all of its blood, and leaving all of its blood is a disqualification from the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this is a rabbinic decree. Planning to leave all of the blood is פסול from the Torah, so חכמים also made planning to leave part of it פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If someone plans to leave all the blood until tomorrow, the blood never gets put on the מזבח, and that is פסול מדאורייתא. Leaving only some of the blood is not פסול from the Torah. חכמים made it פסול anyway, so that people would not treat the full case lightly.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made as a safeguard

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how רבי יהודה can say 'everyone agrees.' The rule is a safeguard based on a Torah-level case, not part of the disagreement about strange uses.

phrases.english: It is a decree regarding some of its blood
because of all of its blood,
and all of its blood is a disqualification by Torah law.

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּזֵירָה מִקְצָת דָּמוֹ אַטּוּ כׇּל דָּמוֹ
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is a rabbinic גזירה: leaving some of the blood is made פסול because of leaving all of it, which is פסול מדאורייתא.

steps.title: A ברייתא: רבי יהודה's argument to חכמים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows רבי יהודה arguing with חכמים. If actually leaving the blood until tomorrow makes it פסול, then planning to leave it is also פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי יהודה said to them: Don't you agree with me that if he left it until tomorrow, it is unfit? So if he planned to leave it until tomorrow, it is also unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as a source for רבי יהודה's view that planning to leave the blood makes the offering פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה uses something חכמים already agree to: blood actually left overnight is פסול. From there he argues that a plan to do the same thing should also make it פסול. This shows that, for him, 'leaving' is a separate case from the strange-use cases.

keyTerms.meaning: He intended, he had in mind

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Yehuda said to them:
Do you not agree with me
that if he left it until the next day, it is unfit?
phrases.notes: He means the blood was really left overnight without being put on the מזבח.

phrases.english: If he intended to leave it until the next day, it is also unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source showing that רבי יהודה rules this way.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה's view that planning to leave the blood until tomorrow makes the offering פסול.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי יהודה argues from the actual leaving of the blood to the intention to leave it.

steps.title: Why רבי אלעזר said 'even in this'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר comes to disagree with רבי יהודה. Even about leaving the blood, רבי אליעזר says פסול and חכמים say כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר came to say: even in this case רבי אליעזר disqualifies and חכמים declare it fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining the purpose of רבי אלעזר's statement. He is answering רבי יהודה's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה said everyone agrees that leaving the blood is פסול. רבי אלעזר's words 'אף בזו' (even in this) mean the argument also covers leaving the blood. So, in his view, חכמים would say כשר here too.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה: everyone agrees that leaving the blood is פסול, because of a rabbinic גזירה. רבי אלעזר: even here רבי אליעזר says פסול and חכמים say כשר.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar comes to say:
even in this case Rabbi Eliezer deems it unfit
and the Rabbis deem it fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי יהודה's view to explain what רבי אלעזר's statement is arguing against.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי אלעזר's 'אף בזו' teaches that the argument between רבי אליעזר and חכמים includes intending to leave the blood, against רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Does רבי יהודה really hold this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether רבי יהודה really holds that everyone agrees leaving the blood is פסול, and starts to bring a ברייתא that seems to show otherwise.
steps.simpleTranslation: And does רבי יהודה really hold that if one intends to leave some of its blood until tomorrow, everyone agrees it is unfit? But it was taught:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the claim it just made about רבי יהודה. It introduces a ברייתא that seems to contradict it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 1 to 4 said that, for רבי יהודה, the leaving case is פסול according to everyone. The גמרא now suspects another source points the other way. The challenge goes straight at that 'everyone agrees' claim.

phrases.english: And does Rabbi Yehuda hold
that to leave some of its blood until the next day
everyone agrees it is unfit?
But isn't it taught:

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לְהַנִּיחַ מִדָּמוֹ לְמָחָר דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל פָּסוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the description of רבי יהודה's view given in steps 1 to 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that, according to רבי יהודה, everyone agrees that intending to leave some of the blood until tomorrow makes the offering פסול.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא about this exact case is about to be quoted, and it appears to conflict with that claim.

steps.title: The story of רבי and יוסף הבבלי
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא begins. רבי tells how he went to learn from רבי אלעזר בן שמוע and found יוסף הבבלי there, who asked about slaughtering with intent to leave some of the blood until tomorrow.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said: When I went to sharpen my learning with רבי אלעזר בן שמוע (some say: to learn from רבי אלעזר בן שמוע), I found יוסף הבבלי sitting before him, and he was very dear to him. Then, about one law, he said to him: רבי, what is the law if one slaughters the offering intending to leave some of its blood until tomorrow?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that backs up its challenge. Here we only hear the setup and the question; the answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא raises the same case: slaughtering with the plan to leave some blood until tomorrow. Since it is asked as an open question, the case does not seem so obvious. The rest of the story will show why this is a problem for the claim about רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: To 'squeeze out my measures,' meaning to sharpen and clarify my learning

phrases.english: Rabbi said:
phrases.notes: 'רבי' alone means רבי יהודה הנשיא, who wrote down the משנה.

phrases.english: When I went to clarify my knowledge
phrases.notes: Literally 'to squeeze out my measures,' meaning to test and sharpen what he had learned.

phrases.english: with Rabbi Elazar ben Shammua,
and some say: to clarify the knowledge
of Rabbi Elazar ben Shammua,
I found Yosef the Babylonian sitting before him,
and it was especially dear to him,
phrases.notes: Each teaching of רבי אלעזר בן שמוע was very precious to יוסף הבבלי.

phrases.english: until, about one matter, he said to him:
My teacher, one who slaughters the offering
intending to leave some of its blood for the next day, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the text of the ברייתא introduced by 'והתניא' in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: The challenge against the claim that רבי יהודה holds everyone agrees leaving the blood is פסול.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי tells of יוסף הבבלי asking רבי אלעזר בן שמוע about slaughtering with intent to leave some blood until tomorrow.

steps.title: Yosef asks again and again until he hears that רבי אליעזר says פסול
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן שמוע answers 'כשר' five times. On the last time he adds that רבי אליעזר says פסול, and יוסף הבבלי's face lights up.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Fit. In the evening he asked again, and he said: Fit. In the morning: Fit. At noon: Fit. In the late afternoon he said: Fit, but רבי אליעזר says it is unfit. יוסף הבבלי's face lit up with joy.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues the story. רבי אלעזר בן שמוע keeps ruling 'כשר' on יוסף הבבלי's question, and only at the end mentions that רבי אליעזר disagrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יוסף keeps asking because the answer 'כשר' doesn't match what he learned. The moment he hears that someone, רבי אליעזר, says פסול, he is happy. This detail is what the גמרא will build its proof on.

keyTerms.meaning: Evening, morning, noon, late afternoon. The times יוסף asked again
His face lit up with joy

phrases.english: He said to him: It is fit.
phrases.notes: This is רבי אלעזר בן שמוע answering יוסף's question from the last step about planning to leave the blood until tomorrow.

phrases.english: In the evening, he said to him: It is fit.
In the morning, he said to him: It is fit.
At noon, he said to him: It is fit.
In the late afternoon, he said to him: It is fit,
but Rabbi Eliezer rules it unfit.
The face of Yosef the Babylonian lit up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא begun in step 7 with רבי אלעזר בן שמוע's answers.
steps.raayaObject: Whether רבי יהודה taught that everyone agrees the offering is פסול.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of יוסף הבבלי and רבי אלעזר בן שמוע.

steps.title: Yosef explains why he was so happy
steps.stepSummary: יוסף says רבי יהודה taught him 'פסול', and no other student backed him up. Now that he hears that some say פסול, his lost teaching has been returned.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Yosef, it seems to me that our teachings were not accurate until now. He answered: רבי, yes! But רבי יהודה taught me 'unfit', and I went around to all his students looking for someone who heard the same, and I found no one. Now that you have taught me 'unfit', you have returned my lost item to me.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר בן שמוע notices יוסף's joy and says his own answers until now may not have been accurate. יוסף explains that he had learned 'פסול' from רבי יהודה and finally found support for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יוסף was afraid he had remembered רבי יהודה's teaching wrong, since none of the other students knew it. Hearing that רבי אליעזר says פסול proves his memory was correct. The key words for the coming proof are 'הֶחְזַרְתָּ לִי אֲבֵידָתִי'.

keyTerms.meaning: Our teachings, the traditions we received
A companion. Here, another student who heard the same teaching
A lost item. Here, a teaching he thought he had lost

phrases.english: He said to him: Yosef,
it seems to me that we did not get accurate
our teachings until now.
phrases.notes: He is talking about himself as 'we'. Seeing יוסף so happy, he senses his answers until now weren't the whole picture.

phrases.english: He said to him: My teacher, yes!
phrases.notes: יוסף is saying he does accept your ruling of כשר.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שֶׁרַבִּי יְהוּדָה פָּסוּל שָׁנָה לִי,
phrases.english: But Rabbi Yehuda taught me 'unfit',
and I went around to all his students
and looked for a companion, and I did not find one.
Now that you have taught me 'unfit',
you have returned my lost item to me.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: יוֹסֵף, כִּמְדוּמֶּה אֲנִי שֶׁלֹּא כִּיוַּונְנוּ שְׁמוּעָתֵינוּ עַד עָתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the joy described at the end of step 8.
steps.raayaObject: What exactly רבי יהודה taught יוסף.
steps.raayaSupportSource: יוסף's words in the ברייתא: 'הֶחְזַרְתָּ לִי אֲבֵידָתִי'.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בן שמוע cries and explains where רבי יהודה got it
steps.stepSummary: Moved by יוסף's love of Torah, רבי אלעזר בן שמוע praises him with a פסוק. He explains that רבי יהודה learned the 'פסול' view from his father רבי אלעאי, a student of רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Tears streamed from the eyes of רבי אלעזר בן שמוע. He said: Happy are you, Torah scholars, for whom words of Torah are so very dear! He applied to him the verse: 'How I love Your Torah; all day it is my conversation.' He explained: Since רבי יהודה is the son of רבי אלעאי, and רבי אלעאי was the student of רבי אליעזר, he taught you the teaching of רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with רבי אלעזר בן שמוע praising יוסף and tracing the chain of tradition from רבי אליעזר to רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר בן שמוע explains why רבי יהודה taught 'פסול': it came down to him from רבי אליעזר through his father רבי אלעאי. The fact that a special explanation was needed hints that רבי יהודה taught something unusual. Steps 13 and 14 build on exactly this point.

phrases.english: His eyes streamed with tears,
the eyes of Rabbi Elazar ben Shammua.
He said: Happy are you, Torah scholars,
for whom words of Torah are exceedingly dear.
He applied this verse to him:
"How I love Your Torah;
all day it is my conversation, etc."

phrases.aramaic: הָא מִפְּנֵי שֶׁרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי אִלְעַאי,
phrases.english: This is because Rabbi Yehuda is the son of Rabbi Elai,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אִלְעַאי תַּלְמִידוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר,
phrases.english: and Rabbi Elai is the student of Rabbi Eliezer;

phrases.aramaic: לְפִיכָךְ שָׁנָה לְךָ מִשְׁנַת רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר.
phrases.english: therefore he taught you the teaching of Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.triggerLanguage: זָלְגוּ עֵינָיו דְּמָעוֹת שֶׁל רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן שַׁמּוּעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to יוסף's explanation in step 9 and closes the ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה's 'פסול' is the view of רבי אליעזר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The chain of tradition: רבי אליעזר, then רבי אלעאי, then רבי יהודה.

steps.title: The proof: רבי יהודה taught it as a מחלוקת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that if רבי יהודה had taught 'everyone agrees it is פסול', hearing about a מחלוקת would not have returned יוסף's lost item. This is a challenge, not the final word; step 14 rejects it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you think רבי יהודה taught him that everyone agrees it is unfit, what does 'you returned my lost item' mean? רבי אלעזר בן שמוע only told him there is a disagreement!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now uses the story to complete the challenge it opened in step 6. It argues that יוסף's joy seems to make sense only if רבי יהודה taught him the 'פסול' view as one side of a disagreement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 asked whether רבי יהודה really holds that everyone agrees leaving the blood is פסול. If that were so, יוסף would have learned 'everyone says פסול'. Hearing 'רבי אליעזר says פסול, others say כשר' would then seem not to give him back his teaching. The גמרא will test the other option in steps 12–13 and then answer this challenge in step 14.

keyTerms.meaning: It enters your mind; if you were to think

steps.whatToRemember: This challenge argues from יוסף's words 'הֶחְזַרְתָּ לִי אֲבֵידָתִי' that רבי יהודה did not teach 'everyone agrees'. Step 14 rejects that reading.
steps.confusionAlert: יוסף was not happy because the הלכה is פסול. He was happy because someone confirmed that a 'פסול' opinion exists, which matched what רבי יהודה had taught him.

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that he taught him 'everyone agrees it is unfit',
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי יהודה and 'him' is יוסף הבבלי.

phrases.english: what is 'you returned my lost item to me'?
He was telling him a disagreement!
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי אלעזר בן שמוע, who only said that רבי אליעזר disagrees.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל פָּסוּל אַתְנְיֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the challenge's conclusion from the ברייתא told in steps 7–10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יהודה holds everyone agrees that leaving the blood is פסול.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: יוסף's 'lost item' was returned by hearing about a disagreement, so what רבי יהודה taught him must itself have been a disagreement, not unanimous agreement.

steps.title: Maybe he taught both opinions?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי יהודה taught a מחלוקת: the רבנן say כשר and רבי אליעזר says פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: So what did רבי יהודה teach? Did he teach that it is כשר, but רבי אליעזר says it is פסול?
steps.whatsHappening: Step 11 challenged the idea that רבי יהודה taught 'everyone agrees'. So the גמרא now tries another option: maybe he taught it as a מחלוקת. This sets up the next challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יהודה taught a מחלוקת, then hearing about a מחלוקת really would give יוסף back what he had lost. This suggestion seems to fit step 11 well.

keyTerms.meaning: So what, then? A way of offering another option

phrases.english: Rather, what [did he teach]?
Did he teach him: 'fit, but Rabbi Eliezer rules it unfit'?
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some leave it out. Both words mean the same thing here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new reading after step 11 ruled out 'everyone agrees'.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Did רבי יהודה teach the case as a מחלוקת between the רבנן and רבי אליעזר?

steps.title: Then why explain where he learned it?
steps.stepSummary: If רבי יהודה taught a normal מחלוקת, there was no need for רבי אלעזר בן שמוע to explain that he got it from his father, a student of רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why did he say it was because of the מחלוקת? We also teach that מחלוקת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggestion in step 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 10, רבי אלעזר בן שמוע gave a special reason for רבי יהודה's teaching: he learned it from his father רבי אלעאי. But רבי אלעזר בן שמוע himself also teaches the מחלוקת. So if רבי יהודה only taught the מחלוקת, nothing would need explaining.

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, מַאי הָא מִפְּנֵי פְּלוּגְתָּא?
phrases.english: If so, what is this 'because of the dispute'?
phrases.notes: This points back to step 10, where he explained that רבי יהודה learned it from his father, a student of רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: We too teach the dispute!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, מַאי הָא מִפְּנֵי פְּלוּגְתָּא
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רבי יהודה taught a מחלוקת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A plain מחלוקת needs no special explanation, but רבי אלעזר בן שמוע did give a special explanation.

steps.title: He taught 'everyone agrees'; יוסף was happy that any פסול view exists
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה really did teach 'everyone agrees it is פסול'. יוסף's 'lost item' was returned because he learned that at least someone holds פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, he taught him that everyone agrees it is פסול. What does 'you returned my lost item' mean? It means he at least gave back to him that some opinion of פסול exists in the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the first reading and explains יוסף's words in a softer way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 asked how hearing about a מחלוקת could return יוסף's teaching if he had learned 'everyone agrees'. The answer is that he did not get back his exact teaching, but he learned that a פסול view really exists, which was enough since no other student of רבי יהודה could confirm it. This also fits step 13: a unanimous 'פסול' is unusual enough to need the explanation about רבי אלעאי.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually; going back to the original idea

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה taught 'everyone agrees it is פסול'. יוסף הבבלי was satisfied just to hear that some opinion of פסול exists.

phrases.english: Rather, actually
he taught him 'everyone agrees it is unfit,'
and what is 'you returned my lost item'?
that he at least gave back to him
phrases.notes: Some versions say the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. The meaning is the same.

phrases.english: some opinion of unfitness in the world.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the reading that step 11 challenged and answers that challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the words 'you returned my lost item'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Returned my lost item' means he got back exactly the teaching he had learned.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means only that he learned some opinion of פסול exists, even though others say כשר.

steps.title: New משנה: missed steps that do not ruin the מנחה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists steps of the מנחה. If any of them is not done, the מנחה is still כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If he did not pour, did not mix, did not break into pieces, did not salt, did not wave, did not bring it near, broke it into pieces that were too big, or did not smear it with oil, the מנחה is כשרה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists steps of preparing a מנחה, and says that missing any of them does not make the מנחה פסולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are the normal steps of the מנחה: pouring oil, mixing, breaking, salting, waving, bringing to the מזבח, and smearing wafers with oil. The משנה says none of them stops the מנחה from being כשרה. The גמרא will soon ask how that can be true for steps the תורה treats as a must.

phrases.english: MISHNA: If he did not pour, did not mix,
and did not break into pieces, and did not salt,
and did not wave, did not bring near,
or he broke them into pieces that were too big,
and did not smear them with oil, it is fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה; the story of יוסף הבבלי is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Missing pouring, mixing, breaking, salting, waving, bringing, or smearing, or breaking into pieces that are too big, does not make the מנחה פסולה.

steps.title: What does 'did not pour' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the משנה means by 'did not pour'.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What does 'did not pour' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking what the first case of the משנה means. This sets up the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question hints that the simple reading, that no one poured at all, may be a problem.

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is 'did not pour'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the first case of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What case is meant by 'did not pour'?

steps.title: Not pouring at all cannot be כשר
steps.stepSummary: If it means that no one poured at all, that cannot be right, because the תורה makes pouring a must.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means he did not pour at all, that is a problem: the תורה writes that pouring is a must.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the simple reading and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pouring the oil is something the מנחה cannot do without. So a מנחה with no pouring at all would be פסולה, and the משנה cannot be talking about that case.

keyTerms.meaning: Something that holds back; a must, without which the מנחה is פסולה

phrases.english: If you say he did not pour at all,
it is written as a must!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries the simple answer to step 16 and rejects it.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading 'did not pour' as 'no pouring at all'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Pouring is a must, so missing it completely would make the מנחה פסולה, not כשרה.

steps.title: A זר poured instead of a כהן
steps.stepSummary: The משנה means that a כהן did not pour; a זר did the pouring.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, a כהן did not pour, but a זר did.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct reading: the pouring was done, but not by a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pouring itself, which is the must, still happened. The only change is who did it. So the משנה is teaching that pouring does not need a כהן.

phrases.english: Rather, a priest did not pour,
but a non-priest [did].

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, לֹא יָצַק כֹּהֵן, אֶלָּא זָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem raised in step 17.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No pouring was done at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: Pouring was done by a זר, and that is כשר.

steps.title: Same reading for mixing: not mixing at all would be פסול
steps.stepSummary: Read the same way, 'did not mix' means a זר mixed. That implies that not mixing at all makes the מנחה פסולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, 'did not mix' also means a כהן did not mix, but a זר did. That shows that if no one mixed at all, the מנחה is פסולה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the same reading to the next case in the משנה and draws a conclusion from it. This sets up the discussion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'did not pour' means pouring by a זר, then 'did not mix' must also mean mixing by a זר. So the משנה only allows mixing by a זר. It does not allow skipping the mixing completely, and that would be פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: This implies; from here we learn

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying that mixing needs a כהן. It says a זר may mix, but the mixing itself must happen.

phrases.english: If so, 'did not mix' also
means a priest did not mix, but a non-priest [did];
this implies that if he did not mix at all, it is unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries step 18's reading over to the next case in the משנה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: By this reading, mixing by a זר is כשר, but a מנחה with no mixing at all is פסולה.
